entities.summary:
Akshardham Temple (Swaminarayan Akshardham) in New Delhi is the world's largest Hindu temple complex, opened in 2005. Built by the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Sanstha (BAPS) organization, it was constructed by 11,000 artisans and volunteers who hand-carved 20,000 intricate sculptures in pink Rajasthani sandstone and Italian marble without using steel or concrete in the main monument.

The central monument, 110 meters wide, 97 meters long, and 43 meters high, is encircled by 234 ornate carved pillars, 9 intricately carved domes, and sculptures depicting flora, fauna, dancers, musicians, and deities from Hindu tradition. The complex includes an IMAX theater showing the 'Mystic India' film about the child saint Neelkanth, a musical fountain show, a boat ride through 10,000 years of India's cultural history, and extensive gardens.

Akshardham was designated a Guinness World Record holder for largest Hindu temple in 2005. The 2008 terrorist attack on the temple (killing 32 people) became a defining incident in the history of Hindu-Muslim tensions in India. Prime Minister Modi, associated with BAPS, participated in the 2023 consecration of a similar Akshardham temple in Robbinsville, New Jersey, built by the same community in the United States, demonstrating the BAPS diaspora's cultural influence.
